level_named: Unspecified - whatever level 'reproduces the causes and not merely describes them'
note: Cuda's n. 1 (p. 126) complains Searle never says what components must share with neurons beyond 'something to do with biochemistry'

level_named: Circuit functional equivalence: the functional role of each neuron
note: Stated as the finest grain and the only one at which sufficiency is claimed; explicitly does not establish sufficiency at any coarser level

level_named: Fine enough to determine the system's behavioural dispositions; 'in the brain, it is likely that the neural level suffices'
note: A coarser level 'might also work'; the grain is set by what fixes behaviour, not by biology

level_named: Causal topology at a level 'fine enough to determine the causation of behavior'; for the brain 'probably the neural level or higher'
note: The notion is conceded to be 'necessarily informal for now'

level_named: Combinatorial-state-automaton substates, each corresponding to 'a distinct physical region in the system'
note: Section 7 admits the distinct-region requirement may be too strong (virtual memory) while dropping independence collapses CSA implementation into FSA implementation

level_named: Individual synapses: structural replication 'in suitably fine-grained detail, such as on the level of individual synapses'
note: The weakest version anyone needs; chemicals affect experience only via their influence on computational activity

level_named: Machine-table individuation, rejected as simultaneously too coarse and too fine
note: One state at a time and a finite list on one side; 'damn' versus 'darn' making two pains type-distinct on the other

level_named: Functional equivalence declared relative to a level of abstractness, with the fatal step located at the input-output interface
note: Physical descriptions of inputs and outputs are chauvinist; descriptions purely as inputs and outputs are liberal; disjunction and mental vocabulary are both barred

level_named: Mechanistic: components with functions, organised - with a stored program a physical part of the machine
note: The grain is whatever neuroscience finds; the paper's point is that the question is empirical rather than settled in advance

level_named: Medium-independent vehicles whose functionally relevant properties are spike rate and spike timing - neither digits nor continuous magnitudes
note: Neural computation is sui generis, so a digital or analog abstraction of it is the wrong grain by construction

level_named: Equivalence classes of physical states, defined by 'input values that lead to uniform behaviour of the whole device'
note: Chosen to make cushion intervals and noise bands irrelevant while preserving equivalence across electronic and hydraulic media

level_named: The level at which a semantic task is specified - content-bearing inputs and outputs
note: Only mathematical or formal content individuates; a brown-cow cell and a black-dog cell share a computational identity

level_named: Whatever level fixes representational content, which may be broad and environment-involving
note: If content is broad, two intrinsic duplicates in different environments are not running the same computation, so grain cannot be read off the system alone

level_named: No synchronic level suffices: content is fixed by selection history, not by present structure
note: Parameter-identical systems computing the same function differ in whether their states represent; an orthogonal constraint rather than a finer or coarser setting

level_named: A definite spatio-temporal grain - the one at which integrated information is maximal; for human experience roughly 100 ms
note: The grain is derived from the exclusion postulate rather than chosen; a mechanism cannot have effects at a fine grain and additional effects at a coarser one

level_named: The maximal substrate: the definite set of units and grain maximising system integrated information
note: Many overlapping sets may have positive integrated information; only the maximum counts, which is stricter than the gloss used by some critics

level_named: The level of information-processing computations: global availability (C1) and self-monitoring (C2)
note: Explicitly 'resolutely computational'; information-theoretic quantities alone are said not to suffice without the nature and depth of what is processed

level_named: The level of an internal model of attention - a deliberately inaccurate schema, not the attention mechanism itself
note: Declared buildable with current technology; a differently architected system would build a different self-model and need not claim consciousness

level_named: The input-output level: 'consciousness must be described in terms of what it does, and not how it does it'
note: The conclusion drawn from the unfolding construction; global workspace, higher-order and predictive-processing theories are exempted by name

level_named: Marr's algorithmic and representational level - neither the implementation level nor the input-output function
note: Explicitly denies that systems computing the same input-output function are alike in consciousness, citing Sprevak 2007

level_named: Sub-neuronal: dual-compartment layer 5 pyramidal neurons and metabotropic receptors 'not usually modeled in artificial neural networks'
note: The stated position is that consciousness may be implementable but at a specificity beyond present and perhaps future AI

level_named: No bottom: 'the imperative to stay alive doesn't bottom out at any particular implementation level in our biology'
note: Proposes causal and informational closure measures to determine empirically how far neural dynamics can be abstracted from finer levels (section 3.5)

level_named: Metabolic activity counted as part of a human agent's functional profile
note: Aimed at the thought experiment rather than the thesis: holding function fixed while removing life may be ill-formed

level_named: Distinguishes being a model from having a model - whether a generative model must be explicitly encoded or only behaved as if
note: Framed as possibly mattering for what selfhood is like; the paper poses it as an outstanding question rather than answering it

level_named: A four-rung ladder of abstraction; only the top rung - a counterfactual or informational connection with no causal chain - is denied
note: Substrate independence at the level of causal processes is conceded: 'the silicon brain and the hydraulic brain may, for all we have said, be conscious' (p. 429)

level_named: An architecture's primitive operations and the process actually running, not the mathematical function computed
note: Any computable function can be made a single primitive, so a function-level criterion makes an extended conscious episode a structureless one-step computation

level_named: The specificity problem: the grain cannot be read off the human experiments the theory was built on
note: Conservatism restricts consciousness to humans; liberalism certifies network time protocol as global information sharing

level_named: Places 'the scale of functional organization that matters' inside the zone of reasonable disagreement and routes around it
note: Advises looking for ways forward that do not rely on controversial assumptions about the grain; his third AI pathway nonetheless uses a minimal global workspace

level_named: Organisational: 'what matters is how neurons or silicon chips are hooked up to each other, not what they are made of'
note: The grain is left open; the paper works instead through six architectural features and assigns each a credence

level_named: A small artificial component 'that contributes identically to the entity's psychology'
note: Assumed rather than argued: n. 5 distinguishes this from Cuda and Chalmers, who try to establish that consciousness survives replacement

level_named: Assigns a credence to computational functionalism itself rather than naming a grain
note: Illustrative arithmetic: a 30-50% chance the thesis holds times a 30-50% chance a given system qualifies gives 9-25%
